title: Vitamins, Minerals, and Water Requirements
text:
4. Vitamins - vitamins are organic compounds needed in minute amounts that are essential for life. In normal condition micro-organism synthesize vitamins K and B-complex in the rumen.
Vitamin A - comes primarily from B-carotene which is abundant in fresh forages.
Vitamin D - is necessary for the absorption and metabolism of calcium and phosphorus. Cholecalciferol (D3) can be formed by the solar irradiation of the skin.
Vitamin E - is very high in fresh forages.

5. Minerals - Needed for bone and teeth formation, hormone actions, enzyme activation and water balance and milk production.

Macro minerals | Micro minerals
Calcium | Iron
Phosphorous | Copper
Magnesium | Manganese
Sodium | Zinc
Chlorine | Iodine
Sulfur | Cobalt
Potassium | Selenium

6. Water - is required in the largest amount by the dairy cow. A lactating cow needs at least 85-90 liters of water every day.

Provide dairy cow ad libitum of water

facts: Vitamins are organic compounds needed in minute amounts that are essential for life.
Under normal conditions, microorganisms synthesize vitamins K and B-complex in the rumen.
Vitamin A comes primarily from B-carotene (beta-carotene), which is abundant in fresh forages.
Vitamin D is necessary for the absorption and metabolism of calcium and phosphorus.
Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) can be formed by the solar irradiation of the skin.
Vitamin E is very high in fresh forages.
Minerals are needed for bone and teeth formation, hormone actions, enzyme activation, water balance, and milk production.
Macro minerals listed include Calcium, Phosphorous, Magnesium, Sodium, Chlorine, Sulfur, and Potassium.
Micro minerals listed include Iron, Copper, Manganese, Zinc, Iodine, Cobalt, and Selenium.
Water is required in the largest amount by the dairy cow.
A lactating dairy cow needs at least 85-90 liters of water every day.
Dairy cows should be provided water ad libitum.
